title.zh: 卷八十九 列傳第十九: 耶律庶成 楊佶 耶律韓留 楊佶 耶律和尚
title.en: Volume 89 Biographies 19: Yelu Shucheng, Yang Ji, Yelu Hanliu, Yang Ji, Yelu Heshang
title.raw: 卷八十九 列傳第十九: 耶律庶成 楊佶 耶律韓留 楊佶 耶律和尚 Volume 89 Biographies 19: Yelu Shucheng, Yang Ji, Yelu Hanliu, Yang Ji, Yelu Heshang

sentences.zh: 耶律庶成

translations.literal: Yelu Shucheng
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Shucheng

sentences.zh: 〈（庶箴 蒲魯）〉

translations.literal: (Shuzhen, Pulu)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Shuzhen and Pulu)]〉

sentences.zh: 楊皙 耶 律韓留 楊佶 耶律和尚

translations.literal: Yang Xi, Yelu Hanliu, Yang Ji, Yelu Heshang
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xi, Yelu Hanliu, Yang Ji, and Yelu Heshang

sentences.zh: 耶律庶成，字喜隱，小字陳六，季父房之後。

translations.literal: Yelu Shucheng, style name Xiyin, childhood name Chenliu, was a descendant of the Shufu branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Shucheng, whose style name was Xiyin and childhood name Chenliu, came from the Shufu branch of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 父吳九，檢校太師。

translations.literal: His father Wu Jiu was an acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wu Jiu held the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 庶成幼好學，書過目不忘。

translations.literal: Shucheng from youth loved learning; what he read he did not forget after one look.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Shucheng loved learning and never forgot a book after a single reading.

sentences.zh: 善遼、漢文字，於詩尤工。

translations.literal: He was skilled in Khitan and Han script; in poetry he was especially accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He was adept in both Khitan and Chinese writing and was especially accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 重熙初，補牌印郎君，累遷樞密直學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongxi era he was appointed Seal and Patent Attendant and was repeatedly promoted to Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongxi reign he entered service as a Seal and Patent Attendant and rose through successive appointments to Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 與蕭韓家奴各進《四時逸樂賦》，帝嗟賞。

translations.literal: He and Xiao Hanjianu each presented "Rhapsodies on Leisure through the Four Seasons," and the emperor sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xiao Hanjianu each submitted Rhapsodies on Leisure through the Four Seasons, which the emperor received with warm admiration.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹醫人鮮知切脈審藥，上命庶成譯方脈書行之，自是人皆通習，雖諸部族亦知醫事。

translations.literal: At first Khitan physicians rarely knew how to take the pulse and judge medicines. The emperor ordered Shucheng to translate books on pulse diagnosis and circulate them; from then on everyone learned them, and even the various tribes came to know medical matters.
translations.idiomatic: At first Khitan physicians seldom knew pulse diagnosis or how to judge medicines. The emperor ordered Shucheng to translate works on pulse lore and put them into practice, after which the art became widely known, and even the tribal peoples learned medical practice.

sentences.zh: 時入禁中，參決疑議。

translations.literal: At the time he entered the inner palace to take part in resolving doubtful questions.
translations.idiomatic: He was regularly summoned into the inner palace to help settle doubtful matters.

sentences.zh: 偕林牙蕭韓家奴等撰《實錄》及《禮書》。

translations.literal: Together with Grand Preceptor Xiao Hanjianu and others he compiled the Veritable Records and the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Grand Preceptor Xiao Hanjianu and others, he compiled the Veritable Records and the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 與樞密副使蕭德修定法令，上詔庶成曰：「方今法令輕重不倫。

translations.literal: With Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xiao Dexiu he revised the statutes. The emperor issued an edict to Shucheng saying: "At present the statutes' severity and leniency are not in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Working with Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xiao Dexiu, he revised the statutes. The emperor addressed Shucheng: "At present the penalties in our statutes are inconsistent in severity.

sentences.zh: 法令者，為政所先，人命所系，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Statutes are what government puts first and what human lives depend on; they cannot be treated without care.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes come first in government and bind human lives; they must be handled with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 卿其審度輕重，從宜修定。」

translations.literal: You should examine severity and leniency and revise them as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Weigh severity and leniency and revise them as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 庶成參酌古今，刊正訛謬，成書以進。

translations.literal: Shucheng weighed past and present, corrected errors, completed the book, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Shucheng drew on past and present models, corrected errors, completed the work, and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而善之。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed it and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and expressed his approval.

sentences.zh: 庶成方進用，為妻胡篤所誣，以罪奪官，絀為「庶耶律」。

translations.literal: Just as Shucheng was rising in favor, he was slandered by his wife Hu Du, stripped of office for a crime, and demoted in clan standing to "Commoner Yelu."
translations.idiomatic: Just as Shucheng was coming into high favor, his wife Hu Du slandered him; he was stripped of office for a crime and reduced in clan rank to the humiliating designation "Commoner Yelu."

sentences.zh: 使吐蕃凡十二年，清寧間始歸。

translations.literal: He was sent to Tibet for twelve years in all and did not return until the Qingning era.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Tibet for twelve years and did not return until the Qingning reign.

sentences.zh: 帝知其誣，詔復本族，仍遷所奪官，卒。

translations.literal: The emperor knew he had been slandered, issued an edict restoring him to his original clan, and also restored the offices that had been taken from him; then he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew he had been wronged, ordered his clan status restored, reinstated the offices that had been stripped from him, and shortly afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 庶成嘗為林牙，夢善卜者胡呂古卜曰：「官止林牙，因妻得罪。」

translations.literal: When Shucheng had served as Grand Preceptor, he dreamed that the skilled diviner Hu Lugu divined for him, saying: "Your office will stop at Grand Preceptor; you will offend because of your wife."
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Grand Preceptor, Shucheng dreamed that the skilled diviner Hu Lugu told his fortune: "Your rank will go no higher than Grand Preceptor, and you will fall because of your wife."

sentences.zh: 及置於理，法當離婚。

translations.literal: When the matter was brought before the law, by statute he ought to divorce.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was brought to judgment, the law required divorce.

sentences.zh: 胡篤適有娠，至期不產而死。

translations.literal: Hu Du happened to be pregnant; when the term came she did not give birth and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Du happened to be pregnant, but when her term came she failed to deliver and died.

sentences.zh: 剖視之，其子以手抱心，識者謂誣夫之報。

translations.literal: When they cut her open and looked, the child was clasping its heart with its hands; those who knew said this was retribution for slandering her husband.
translations.idiomatic: On dissection the child was found clutching its own heart in its hands, which observers took as retribution for her false accusation against her husband.

sentences.zh: 有詩文行於世。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 弟庶箴。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Shuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Shuzhen.

sentences.zh: 庶箴，字陳甫，善屬文。

translations.literal: Shuzhen, style name Chenfu, was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhen, whose style name was Chenfu, was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 重熙中，為本族將軍。

translations.literal: During the Chongxi era he served as general of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongxi reign he served as general of his clan.

sentences.zh: 咸雍元年，同知東京留守事，俄徙烏衍突厥部節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianyong he became associate Eastern Capital regent; before long he was transferred to military commissioner of the Wuyan Tujue tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianyong he became associate Eastern Capital regent and was soon transferred to military commissioner of the Wuyan Tujue tribe.

sentences.zh: 九年，知薊州事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he administered Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he took charge of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷都林牙。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Chief Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to chief grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 上表乞廣本國姓氏曰：「我朝創業以來，法制修明；

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting expansion of the national surnames, saying: "Since our dynasty's founding, institutions and laws have been well ordered;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting expansion of the national surnames, saying, "Since our dynasty's founding, institutions and laws have been well ordered;

sentences.zh: 惟姓氏止分為二，耶律與蕭而已。

translations.literal: surnames are divided into only two, Yelu and Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: surnames are divided into only two, Yelu and Xiao.

sentences.zh: 始太祖制契丹大字，取諸部鄉里之名，續作一篇，著於卷末。

translations.literal: At the outset the Taizu devised the great Khitan script, taking names from the townships and villages of the various tribes; he composed a further piece and placed it at the end of the roll.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Taizu devised the great Khitan script, taking names from the townships and villages of the various tribes, composed a further piece, and placed it at the end of the roll.

sentences.zh: 臣請推廣之，使諸部各立姓氏，庶男女婚媾有合典禮。」

translations.literal: I request that this be extended, so that each tribe may establish its own surname, and that men's and women's marriages may conform to ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: I request that this be extended so each tribe may establish its own surname and men's and women's marriages may conform to ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 帝以舊制不可遽厘，不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor held that the old system could not be abruptly changed and did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that the old system could not be abruptly changed and did not assent.

sentences.zh: 大康二年，出耶律乙辛為中京留守，庶箴與耶律孟簡表賀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dakang, Yelü Yixin was sent out as commissioner of the Central Capital; Shuzhen together with Yelü Mengjian submitted a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dakang, Yelü Yixin was sent out as commissioner of the Central Capital; Shuzhen and Yelü Mengjian submitted a congratulatory memorial.

sentences.zh: 頃之，乙辛復為樞密使，專權恣虐。

translations.literal: Before long Yixin returned as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and wielded power arbitrarily with cruel abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yixin returned as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and wielded power arbitrarily with cruel abuse.

sentences.zh: 庶箴私見乙辛泣曰：「前抗表，非庶箴之願也。」

translations.literal: Shuzhen privately visited Yixin and wept, saying: "My earlier memorial opposing him was not Shuzhen's true wish."
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhen privately visited Yixin and wept, saying, "My earlier memorial opposing him was not Shuzhen's true wish."

sentences.zh: 乙辛信其言，乃得自安。

translations.literal: Yixin believed his words and was thus able to feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin believed him and was thus able to feel secure.

sentences.zh: 聞者鄙之。

translations.literal: Those who heard of it despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard of it despised him.

sentences.zh: 八年，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he retired from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 子蒲魯。

translations.literal: His son was Pulu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Pulu.

sentences.zh: 蒲魯，字乃展。

translations.literal: Pulu, style name Naizhan.
translations.idiomatic: Pulu, whose style name was Naizhan,

sentences.zh: 幼聰悟好學，甫七歲，能誦契丹大字。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and loved learning; at only seven he could recite the great Khitan script.
translations.idiomatic: was clever and studious from childhood; at only seven he could recite the great Khitan script.

sentences.zh: 習漢文，未十年，博通經籍。

translations.literal: He studied Han writing, and in less than ten years he thoroughly mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Chinese writing and within less than ten years had mastered the classical canon.

sentences.zh: 重熙中，舉進士第。

translations.literal: During the Chongxi era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongxi reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 主文以國制無契丹試進士之條，聞於上，以庶箴擅令子就科目，鞭之二百。

translations.literal: The chief examiner, because the national regulations had no provision for Khitan candidates in the jinshi examination, reported it to the emperor; Shuzhen was held to have presumptuously allowed his son to enter the examination category and was flogged two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: The chief examiner reported to the throne that national law contained no provision for Khitans to sit the jinshi examination. Shuzhen was judged to have presumptuously placed his son in the examination and was given two hundred strokes of the whip.

sentences.zh: 尋命莆魯為牌印郎君。

translations.literal: Before long Pulu was appointed Seal and Patent Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Pulu was appointed Seal and Patent Attendant.

sentences.zh: 應詔賦詩，立成以進。

translations.literal: When summoned to compose poetry at imperial command, he finished it on the spot and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: When called upon to compose verse at imperial command, he finished a poem on the spot and presented it.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉賞，顧左右曰：「文才如此，必不能武事。」

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and, turning to those at his side, said: "With literary talent like this, he surely cannot handle military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and remarked to his attendants, "With literary talent like this, he surely cannot be skilled in arms."

sentences.zh: 蒲魯奏曰：「臣自蒙義方，兼習騎射，在流輩中亦可周旋。」

translations.literal: Pulu memorialized: "Your servant from childhood has received proper instruction and has also practiced riding and archery; among my peers I can still hold my own."
translations.idiomatic: Pulu replied, "Your servant has been properly instructed from youth and has also trained in riding and archery; among my peers I can still hold my own."

sentences.zh: 帝未之信。

translations.literal: The emperor did not yet believe him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was not yet convinced.

sentences.zh: 會從獵，三矢中三兔，帝奇之，轉通進。

translations.literal: On one occasion when he accompanied a hunt, three arrows hit three hares; the emperor marveled at him and transferred him to Tongjin.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a hunt he brought down three hares with three arrows. The emperor was astonished and promoted him to Tongjin.

sentences.zh: 是時，父庶箴嘗寄《戒諭詩》，蒲魯答以賦，眾稱其典雅。

translations.literal: At that time his father Shuzhen had once sent him an "Admonitory Poem"; Pulu answered with a rhapsody, and everyone praised its elegance.
translations.idiomatic: About that time his father Shuzhen sent him an admonitory poem, to which Pulu replied with a rhapsody that everyone praised for its refinement.

sentences.zh: 寵遇漸隆。

translations.literal: Favor toward him gradually rose.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favor toward him steadily increased.

sentences.zh: 清寧初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Qingning era.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Qingning reign.

sentences.zh: 楊皙，字昌時，安次人。

translations.literal: Yang Xi, style name Changshi, was a man of Anci.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xi, whose style name was Changshi, was a native of Anci.

sentences.zh: 幼通《五經》大義。

translations.literal: From youth he understood the great meaning of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he grasped the essential meaning of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 聖宗聞其穎悟，詔試講，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Shengzong heard of his keen intelligence, ordered him tested in lecturing, and appointed him Collator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shengzong heard of his exceptional intelligence, he ordered a trial lecture and appointed him Collator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太平十一年，擢進士乙科，為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Taiping he was selected in the second class of the jinshi examination and made Assistant Gentleman for Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Taiping era he passed the jinshi examination in the second class and was appointed Assistant Gentleman for Compilation.

sentences.zh: 重熙十二年，累遷樞密都承旨，權度支使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chongxi he was repeatedly promoted to Chief Secretariat Attendant of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Acting Commissioner of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Chongxi he rose through successive appointments to Chief Secretariat Attendant of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Acting Commissioner of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 登對稱旨，進樞密副使。

translations.literal: In audience his answers matched the emperor's intent, and he was advanced to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His answers in audience pleased the emperor, and he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 歷長寧軍節度使，山西路轉運使，知興中府。

translations.literal: He served as Military Governor of Changning Circuit, Transport Commissioner of the Shanxi Route, and Prefect of Xingzhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military governor of Changning Circuit, transport commissioner of the Shanxi Route, and prefect of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 清寧初，入知南院樞密使，與姚景行同總朝政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingning he entered the court as Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs and, together with Yao Jingxing, jointly oversaw court government.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingning he entered court service as Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs and, together with Yao Jingxing, directed the government.

sentences.zh: 請行柴冊禮。

translations.literal: He requested that the firewood-register rite be performed.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for the performance of the firewood-register enthronement rite.

sentences.zh: 封趙國公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 以足疾，復知興中府。

translations.literal: Because of a foot ailment, he again became Prefect of Xingzhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a foot ailment he returned to serve as prefect of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 咸雍初，徙封齊，召賜同德功臣、尚書左僕射，兼中書令，拜樞密使，改封晉，給宰相、樞密使兩廳傔從，封趙王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianyong his fief was changed to Qi; he was summoned and granted the title Meritous Minister of Shared Virtue, made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Central Secretariat Director, appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, had his fief changed to Jin, was given attendants of both the chancellor's and the commissioner's offices, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianyong his fief was transferred to Qi. Summoned to court, he received the title Meritous Minister of Shared Virtue, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent appointment as Central Secretariat Director, and was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. His fief was then changed to Jin, he was granted the attendants allotted to both the chancellor's and the commissioner's offices, and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 屢請歸政，益賜保節功臣，致仕。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested to return power, was further granted the title Meritous Minister Who Preserves Integrity, and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire from government, was further granted the title Meritous Minister Who Preserves Integrity, and left office.

sentences.zh: 大康五年，例改遼西郡王，薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dakang, by precedent his title was changed to Prince of Liaoxi Commandery, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dakang his title was changed by precedent to Prince of Liaoxi Commandery, and he died.

sentences.zh: 耶律韓留，字速寧，仲父隋國王之後。

translations.literal: Yelu Hanliu, style name Suning, was of the younger line of the King of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Hanliu, whose style name was Suning, was of the younger line of the King of Sui.

sentences.zh: 有明識，篤行義，舉止嚴重，工為詩。

translations.literal: He had clear insight, was devoted to righteousness in conduct, dignified in bearing, and accomplished in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He had clear insight, was devoted to righteous conduct, dignified in bearing, and accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 統和間，召攝禦院通進。

translations.literal: During the Tonghe era he was summoned to serve as acting courier of the Imperial Park.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe reign he was summoned to serve as acting courier of the Imperial Park.

sentences.zh: 開泰三年，稍遷烏古敵烈部都監，俄知詳穩事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaitai he was slightly promoted to chief overseer of the Wugu and Dilie tribes; before long he took charge of detail-stable affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaitai he was promoted to chief overseer of the Wugu and Dilie tribes and soon took charge of detail-stable affairs.

sentences.zh: 敵烈部叛，將宮分軍，從樞密使耶律世良討平之，加千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When the Dilie tribe rebelled, he led the palace division forces and, following Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yelu Shiliang, put down the rebellion; he was given the additional title General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dilie tribe rebelled, he led the palace division forces and, following Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yelu Shiliang, put down the rebellion; he received the additional title General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 重熙元年，累遷至同知上京留守，改奚六部禿裏太尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongxi he was repeatedly promoted to associate defender of the Supreme Capital and was changed to Grand Commandant Tuli of the Six Xi Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongxi he rose through successive appointments to associate defender of the Supreme Capital and was reassigned as grand commandant tuli of the Six Xi tribes.

sentences.zh: 性不茍合，為樞密使蕭解裏所忌。

translations.literal: By nature he would not compromise; Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xiao Jieli resented him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he would not compromise, and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xiao Jieli resented him.

sentences.zh: 上欲召用韓留，解裏言目病不能視，議前寢。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to summon Hanliu to office, but Jieli said he had an eye ailment and could not see; the matter was laid aside before discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to summon Hanliu to office, but Jieli said he had an eye ailment and could not see, and the matter was dropped before discussion.

sentences.zh: 四年，召為北面林牙。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as Northern Court linya.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was summoned as Northern Court linya.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕早欲用卿，聞有疾，故待之至今。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I long wished to employ you; hearing you were ill, I waited until now."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I long wished to employ you; hearing you were ill, I waited until now."

sentences.zh: 韓留對曰：「臣昔有目疾，才數月耳；

translations.literal: Hanliu replied: "Your servant formerly had an eye ailment, only a few months in all;
translations.idiomatic: Hanliu replied, "Your servant formerly had an eye ailment, only a few months in all;

sentences.zh: 然料不至於昏。

translations.literal: yet I did not expect it would lead to blindness.
translations.idiomatic: yet I did not expect it would lead to blindness.

sentences.zh: 第臣駑拙，不能事權貴，是以不獲早睹天顏。

translations.literal: Only your servant is dull and clumsy and cannot serve the powerful; therefore I did not obtain an early audience with Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Only your servant is dull and clumsy and cannot serve the powerful; therefore I did not obtain an early audience with Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 非陛下聖察，則愚臣豈有今日耶！」

translations.literal: Had Your Majesty not discerned with sagacity, how could this foolish servant have this day!"
translations.idiomatic: Had Your Majesty not discerned with sagacity, how could this foolish servant have this day!"

sentences.zh: 詔進《述懷詩》，上嘉嘆。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to present "Expressing Feelings," and the emperor sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to present Expressing Feelings, and the emperor sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 方將大用，卒。

translations.literal: Just as he was about to be greatly employed, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to be greatly employed, he died.

sentences.zh: 楊佶，字正叔，南京人。

translations.literal: Yang Ji, style name Zhengshu, was a man of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji, whose style name was Zhengshu, was a native of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟異常，讀書自能成句，識者奇之。

translations.literal: From youth his intelligence was extraordinary; when he read books he could form sentences on his own, and those who knew him marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: As a child his intelligence was extraordinary: when he read he could compose sentences on his own, and observers regarded him as remarkable.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，聲名籍甚。

translations.literal: By his coming of age his reputation was already great.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he came of age his reputation was already widespread.

sentences.zh: 統和二十四年，舉進士第一，歷校書郎、大理正。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Tonghe he took first place in the jinshi examination and served as Collator and as Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Tonghe he placed first in the jinshi examination and served successively as collator and director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 開泰六年，轉儀曹郎，典掌書命，加諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaitai he was transferred to Gentleman of the Bureau of Rites, took charge of written commands, and was given the additional title Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaitai he was transferred to Gentleman of the Bureau of Rites, placed in charge of written commands, and given the additional title Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 出知易州，治尚清簡，征發期會必信。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Yizhou; his administration favored clarity and simplicity, and in levies and scheduled deliveries he was always trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as prefect of Yizhou, he governed with clarity and restraint, and in levies and scheduled deliveries he was always reliable.

sentences.zh: 入為大理少卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 累遷翰林學士，文章號得體。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Academician; his writings were praised as well suited to occasion.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Hanlin Academician, and his writings were praised as always apt in tone.

sentences.zh: 八年，燕地饑疫，民多流殍，以佶同知南京留守事，發倉廩，振乏絕，貧民鬻子者計傭而出之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year famine and pestilence struck the Yan region, and many people wandered off and starved to death; Ji was made Associate Administrator of the Nanjing garrison, opened the granaries, relieved the destitute, and for poor people who had sold their children he calculated wages to redeem them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year famine and pestilence struck the Yan region, and many people died wandering in destitution. Ji was appointed associate administrator of the Nanjing garrison, opened the granaries, and relieved the needy; for poor families who had sold their children, he calculated wages so they could be redeemed.

sentences.zh: 宋遣梅詢賀千齡節，詔佶迎送，多唱酬，詢每見稱賞。

translations.literal: Song sent Mei Xun to congratulate the Thousand-Year Festival; the emperor ordered Ji to receive and escort him; they exchanged many poems in reply, and Xun repeatedly praised him when they met.
translations.idiomatic: When Song sent Mei Xun to congratulate the Thousand-Year Festival, the emperor ordered Ji to receive and escort him. They exchanged many poems in correspondence, and Mei repeatedly praised him in their meetings.

sentences.zh: 復為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He again became Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 重熙元年，升翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongxi he was promoted to Chief Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongxi he was promoted to chief Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復工部尚書。

translations.literal: When his mother died he entered mourning, then was recalled from mourning to serve as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he entered mourning, but was soon recalled to serve as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 歷忠順軍節度使，朔武等州觀察處置使，天德軍節度使，加特進檢校太師、同中書門下平章事，復拜參知政事，兼知南院樞密使。

translations.literal: He served as Military Governor of Zhongshun Circuit, Commissioner for Observation and Disposition of Shuowu and other prefectures, Military Governor of Tiande Army, was given the additional titles of Special Advanced Grand Master and Acting Grand Preceptor with the title Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, was again appointed Participant in Governance, and concurrently served as Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military governor of Zhongshun Circuit, commissioner for observation and disposition of Shuowu and other prefectures, and military governor of the Tiande Army. He received the additional titles Special Advanced Grand Master and Acting Grand Preceptor with the title associate grand councilor, was again appointed participant in governance, and concurrently served as commissioner of the Southern Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十五年，出為武定軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he went out as Military Governor of Wuding Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was posted as military governor of Wuding Circuit.

sentences.zh: 境內亢旱，苗稼將槁。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction there was severe drought, and the grain crops were about to wither.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction suffered severe drought, and the crops were on the verge of withering.

sentences.zh: 視事之夕，雨澤沾足。

translations.literal: On the evening he took up office, rain and moisture were fully sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening he assumed office, rain fell in abundance.

sentences.zh: 百姓歌曰：「何以蘇我？

translations.literal: The common people sang: "By what shall we be revived?
translations.idiomatic: The people sang, "How shall we be revived?

sentences.zh: 上天降雨。

translations.literal: Heaven sends down rain.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends rain.

sentences.zh: 誰其撫我？

translations.literal: Who will comfort us?
translations.idiomatic: Who will care for us?

sentences.zh: 楊公為主。」

translations.literal: Lord Yang is our master."
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yang is our lord."

sentences.zh: 漯陽水失故道，歲為民害，乃以己俸創長橋，人不病涉。

translations.literal: The Luoyang River had lost its old course and every year harmed the people; he therefore used his own salary to build a long bridge, so that people were not troubled in crossing.
translations.idiomatic: The Luoyang River had left its old channel and each year brought harm to the people, so he used his own salary to build a long bridge, sparing travelers the hardship of crossing.

sentences.zh: 及被召，郡民攀轅泣送。

translations.literal: When he was summoned back, the people of the commandery clung to his carriage shafts and wept as they saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: When he was recalled to court, the people of the commandery clung to his carriage and wept as they bade him farewell.

sentences.zh: 上御清涼殿宴勞之，即日除吏部尚書，兼門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor received him in the Qingliang Hall with a feast to console him and that same day appointed him Minister of Personnel, concurrently Vice Director of the Gate Department and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entertained him in the Qingliang Hall to honor his service and that same day appointed him Minister of Personnel with concurrent posts as vice director of the Gate Department and associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿今日何減呂望之遇文王！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How is your reception today any less than Lü Wang's meeting King Wen!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How is the favor shown you today any less than what Lü Wang received from King Wen!"

sentences.zh: 佶對曰：「呂望比臣遭際有十年之晚。」

translations.literal: Ji replied: "Compared with your servant, Lü Wang met his opportunity ten years too late."
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied, "Compared with me, Lü Wang met his opportunity a full ten years too late."

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 其居相位，以進賢為己任，事總大綱，責成百司，人人樂為之用。

translations.literal: When he held the chancellorship, he took advancing the worthy as his own task, kept affairs to the great outlines, held the hundred offices accountable, and everyone was glad to be put to use by him.
translations.idiomatic: In office as chancellor he made advancing worthy men his chief duty, kept to the broad outlines of policy, held every office accountable, and all were glad to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 三請致政，許之，月給錢粟傔隸，四時遣使存問。

translations.literal: Three times he requested to retire from government; permission was granted, and each month he was given money, grain, and attendants; in the four seasons envoys were sent to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: He asked three times to retire from government and was permitted to do so, receiving monthly stipends of money, grain, and attendants, with envoys sent in every season to inquire after his welfare.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 有《登瀛集》行於世。

translations.literal: His Ascending to the Immortal Isles Collection circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collection Ascending to the Immortal Isles circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 耶律和尚，字特抹，系出季父房。

translations.literal: Yelu Heshang, style name Temuo, came from the Shufu branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Heshang, whose style name was Temuo, came from the Shufu branch of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 善滑稽。

translations.literal: He was skilled in witty repartee.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in witty and humorous speech.

sentences.zh: 重熙初，補祗候郎君。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongxi he was appointed Attendant in Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongxi reign he entered service as an attendant in waiting.

sentences.zh: 時帝篤於親親，凡三父之後，皆序父兄行第，於和尚尤狎愛。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was devoted to kinship; all descendants of the three paternal uncles were ranked by their fathers' and elder brothers' generation order, and toward Heshang he was especially intimate and fond.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then deeply devoted to his kinsmen; all descendants of the three paternal uncles were ranked by paternal generation, and he was especially intimate and affectionate toward Heshang.

sentences.zh: 然每侍宴飲，雖詼諧，未嘗有一言之過，由是上益重之。

translations.literal: Yet whenever he attended banquets and drinking, though he was humorous, he never once had a word out of place; because of this the emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever he attended banquets, though playful in manner, he never let a single improper word slip, and for this the emperor esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 歷積慶、永興宮使，累遷至同知南院宣徽使事、南面林牙。

translations.literal: He served as Commissioner of the Jiqing and Yongxing Palaces and was repeatedly promoted to Associate Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and Grand Preceptor of the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commissioner of the Jiqing and Yongxing Palaces and rose through successive appointments to associate commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and grand preceptor of the Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 十六年，出為懷化軍節度使，俄召為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he went out as Military Governor of Huaihua Circuit; before long he was summoned back as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was posted as military governor of Huaihua Circuit and was soon recalled as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，因大冊，加天平軍節度使、檢校太師，徙中京路按問使，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, on the occasion of the great enfeoffment, he was given the additional posts of Military Governor of Tianping Circuit and Acting Grand Preceptor, was transferred to Investigation Commissioner of the Zhongjing Route, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, on the occasion of the great enfeoffment, he received the additional titles military governor of Tianping Circuit and acting grand preceptor, was transferred to investigation commissioner of the Zhongjing Route, and died.

sentences.zh: 和尚雅有美行，數以財恤親友，人皆愛重。

translations.literal: Heshang by nature had fine conduct and often used his wealth to relieve kinsmen and friends; everyone loved and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Heshang was known for his fine character and often used his wealth to help kinsmen and friends; everyone loved and respected him.

sentences.zh: 然嗜酒不事事，以故不獲柄用。

translations.literal: Yet he loved wine and did not attend to affairs, and for this reason did not obtain real power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved wine and neglected official business, and for this reason never gained real authority.

sentences.zh: 或以為言，答曰：「吾非不知，顧人生如風燈石火，不飲將何為？」

translations.literal: When someone spoke to him about it, he answered: "It is not that I do not know; only human life is like a lamp in the wind or a spark on stone—if I do not drink, what shall I do?"
translations.idiomatic: When others remonstrated with him, he replied, "It is not that I do not understand, but human life is like a lamp in the wind or a spark on flint—if I do not drink, what else is there to do?"

sentences.zh: 晚年沈湎尤甚，人稱為「酒仙」云。

translations.literal: In his later years his drowning in drink was especially deep, and people called him the "Wine Immortal."
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he sank even deeper into drink, and people called him the "Wine Immortal."

sentences.zh: 論曰：庶成定法令，治民者不容高下其手。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Shucheng fixed the statutes, so that those who governed the people could not raise or lower their hands at will.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: By fixing the statutes, Shucheng ensured that those who governed the people could not manipulate penalties at will.

sentences.zh: 庶箴雖嘗表請廣姓氏，以秩典禮，其隨勢俯仰，則有愧於其子蒲魯矣。

translations.literal: Although Shuzhen once memorialized requesting expansion of the surname registers to order ritual precedence, in bending with the times he had reason to feel ashamed before his son Pulu.
translations.idiomatic: Although Shuzhen once memorialized to expand the clan registers and set ritual precedence, his readiness to bend with changing fortunes left him shamed before his son Pulu.

sentences.zh: 楊皙為上寵遇，叠封王爵，而功業不少概見。

translations.literal: Yang Xi received the emperor's favor and was repeatedly enfeoffed with princely titles, yet his achievements are scarcely visible in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xi enjoyed the emperor's favor and received repeated enfeoffments as prince, yet his substantive achievements are scarcely to be seen.

sentences.zh: 然得愛民治國之要，其楊佶哉！

translations.literal: Yet in grasping the essentials of loving the people and governing the state—was it not Yang Ji!
translations.idiomatic: Yet in mastering the essentials of caring for the people and governing the realm—surely that was Yang Ji!
